rules.title: Eviction from owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling at end of lease
rules.requirement: A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may be evicted after the lease expires if the landlord has given written notice for delivery of possession. A three-month notice to quit is required for an at will or year-to-year tenancy, and a one-month notice to quit for a month-to-month tenancy.
rules.key_value: three-month notice to quit (at will or year-to-year); one-month notice to quit (month-to-month)
rules.coverage_text: Tenants residing in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: Under this cause of not renewing the lease, a three-month notice to quit must be given if an at will tenancy or year -to year tenancy exists.

rules.title: Three-day notice to quit for disorderly, destructive or rule-violating conduct
rules.requirement: A three-day written Notice to Quit is required before eviction for causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or lease provisions.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants facing eviction for disorderly conduct, destruction, or violation of written rules or lease provisions.
rules.quoted_span: A three-day written Notice to Quit is required for any of the causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or lease provisions (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2(a)).

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau, and must give at least three working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction action.
rules.key_value: at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses: buildings with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms, unless an exception applies.
rules.exemptions: Hotels with more than 85 percent temporary occupancy by people with homes elsewhere, school and college dormitories, buildings housing only college students and certain residences for the disabled; also where otherwise ordered by the Bureau.
rules.quoted_span: There is a further requirement that the owner give at least three (3) working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board before starting the eviction action for any resident  (N.J.A.C. 5:26-3.4(c)).

rules.title: Owner move-in occupancy requirement
rules.requirement: When a tenant vacates after notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit, the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six months; renting to another tenant or registering a condominium or cooperative conversion instead makes the landlord liable to the former tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Units vacated after an owner-occupancy eviction notice.
rules.penalty: Landlord liable to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.

rules.title: Removal from residential use after eviction
rules.requirement: When a tenant vacates after notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up, demolish or retire the building from residential use, the landlord must not use the property for residential use for five years.
rules.coverage_text: Properties where tenants vacated after notice of permanent board-up, demolition or retirement from residential use.
rules.penalty: Liability to the tenant for three (3) times the damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation; property may not be registered as a planned real estate development during the five-year period.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.

rules.title: Foreclosure is not grounds for eviction; 90-day notice to quit
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, a 90-day notice to quit is required when the property is bought by a buyer who wants to occupy it as a primary residence, and a tenant with a longer lease cannot be evicted until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenants in foreclosed properties, including month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units.
rules.citation: Chase Manhattan Bank v. Josephson, 135 N.J. 209 (1994)
rules.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey. In Chase Manhattan Bank v. Josephson, 135 N.J. 209 (1994) the court held that when a lender or other buyer takes possession of the property, the residential tenant comes with the property.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizens and disabled tenants in buildings being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever is greater.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants at least 62 years of age, permanently disabled, or qualifying disabled veterans, who have lived in a building being converted at least one year prior to the conversion recording date.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).
